newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends stable but buyers sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends stable but buyers sidelined.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices saw an easing of midday gains to close unchanged from the previous day's value after buyers remained uninspired to enter the market, traders said.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted May RSS1 at 291.50 cents ($1.16) a kg and May SMR20 buyer at 276.50, both unchanged from Tuesday.
Trading houses quoted the SMR CV at 346 cents, SMR L at 325, SMR 10 at 278 and drum latex at 233-235 cents FOB.
"There was no report of sales," said an official trade source.
He said buyers were shirking the domestic market because its prices were still higher than elsewhere in the region.
Sentiment was also weak despite a tighter supply of raw materials after the recent wintering period.
The INRO five-day moving indicator was quoted at 224.31 Malaysian/Singaporean cents per kg on April 8 from 225.19 on April 7. The daily indicator also ended lower at 222.83 from 223.24 previously.
